Torbay's population increased by around 8,400 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 140,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Torbay increased by 6.4%, from around 131,000 in 2011 to around 139,300 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the South West (7.8%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Torbay was home to around 15.8 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 14.9 in 2011. This area was among the top 30% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Torbay than across the South West

An older Torbay

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Torbay increased by three years, from 46 to 49 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the South West as a whole in 2021 (44 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by just under 3,700 (an increase of 23.5%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 2,700 (10.7% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 1.9 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Disability in Torbay

The age-standardised proportion of non-disabled residents fell in Torbay, but rose across England.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In Torbay, the proportion of non-disabled residents fell from 78.4% in 2011 to 77.9% in 2021, while across England it rose from 80.7% to 82.3%. During the same period, the regional proportion increased from 81.9% to 82.2%.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Torbay fell from 10.4% to 9.9%, while the percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little increased from 11.2% to 12.2%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of non-disabled residents in Torbay decreased by 0.5 percentage points

Unpaid care in Torbay

In 2021, 4.8% of Torbay residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.2% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care was greater across the South West (2.8 percentage points, from 7.5% to 4.7%) than in Torbay (2.4 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Torbay decreased by 2.4 percentage points

Family in Torbay

Torbay saw the South West's joint second-largest percentage-point rise (alongside Wiltshire and East Devon) in the proportion of households including a couple with only non-dependent children (from 4.9% in 2011 to 5.5% in 2021).

Across the region, only Swindon saw a greater rise in the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children (from 5.7% to 6.5%).

Despite the increase, Torbay was in the lowest 15% of English local authority areas for the share of households including a couple with only non-dependent children in 2021.

The percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children in Torbay increased by 0.6 percentage points

People looking after their family or home in Torbay

Torbay saw the South West's joint second-largest percentage-point rise (alongside Swindon) in the proportion of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home (from 3.4% in 2011 to 4.3% in 2021).

Across the region, only Isles of Scilly saw a greater rise in the percentage of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home (from 1.5% to 3.4%).

Because of its small size, comparisons to Isles of Scilly should be made with caution.

Every local authority area across the South West saw a rise in the percentage of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home, as the regional percentage grew from 3.3% to 3.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were looking after their family or home (economically inactive) in Torbay increased by 0.9 percentage points

More adults worked short hours

Torbay saw the South West's third-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week (from 10.2% in 2011 to 11.8% in 2021).

Across the region, only Isles of Scilly (from 7.4% to 12.0%) and South Hams (from 12.4% to 14.5%) saw a greater increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Torbay increased by 1.6 percentage points

Religion in Torbay

In 2021, 43.2% of Torbay residents reported having "No religion", up from 27.5% in 2011. The rise of 15.7 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Torbay. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South West, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 29.3% to 44.1%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 48.5% of people in Torbay described themselves as Christian (down from 63.3%), while 6.3% did not state their religion (down from 7.7% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 43.2% of usual residents in Torbay reported having "No religion"

Torbay residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 124,600 Torbay residents said they were born in England. This represented 89.5% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 118,800 in 2011, which at the time represented 90.8% of Torbay's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with just over 2,200 Torbay residents reporting this country of birth (1.6%). This figure was down from just under 2,400 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.8% of the population of Torbay.

The number of Torbay residents born in Wales fell from around 2,200 in 2011 (1.7% of the local population) to around 2,100 in 2021 (1.5%).

In 2021, 89.5% of Torbay residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Torbay

In 2021, 3.9% of Torbay residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 2.8% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.1% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.4% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Torbay that identified as "British only" increased from 13.5% to 55.5%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the South West (1.7 percentage points, from 4.4% to 6.1%) than in Torbay (1.1 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Torbay increased by 1.1 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Torbay residents aged 16 years and over, 32.8% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 29.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 4 in 10 people (44.2%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 46.9% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Torbay that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 12.2% to 12.6%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Torbay (3.7 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South West (3.5 percentage points, from 31.1% to 34.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Torbay increased by 3.7 percentage points

Change in housing in Torbay

Of Torbay households, 64.1% owned their home in 2021, down from 66.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in four households (26.6%) rented privately, compared with 23.2% in 2011. The percentage of Torbay households that lived in a socially rented property increased from 8.1% to 8.3%.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home was greater in Torbay (2.7 percentage points) than across the South West (1.6 percentage points, from 67.4% to 65.9%). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in Torbay decreased by 2.7 percentage points

Health in Torbay

In 2021, 45.4% of Torbay residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 44.0% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.3% to 33.7%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Torbay residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.4% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 5.3% to 5.0%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Torbay increased by 1.4 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Torbay

In 2021, 1.6% of Torbay residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 1.0% in 2011. The 0.6 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South West, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 2.0% to 2.8%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 96.1% of people in Torbay identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 97.5% in 2011), while 1.5% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.1% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.2% in 2011 to 0.4% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

Read the bulletin Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021.
